FO-138 Safety - Work Gear and Personal Effects (2024-01-11)pw
content: None

SAFETY - WORK GEAR AND
PERSONAL EFFECTS FO-138
OVERVIEW
The purpose of this document is to ensure that you are aware of your responsibility to supply work
clothing and personal effects. Hy-Tech job locations vary and so do the weather conditions and we’d like
to ensure that you are prepared for all situations.

It is important that you closely review this information prior to your departure as you are required to
supply and wear the appropriate work clothing and gear. Employees who do not have the required work
gear will be subject to Hy-Tech’s disciplinary process. Hy-Tech will work with the employee to have the
required work gear sent to the job site at the employee’s expense.

Hy-Tech will provide safety glasses, hard hat, and ear plugs. Refer to POL-02C Employee Policy; Field
(Canadian Employees) to verify other items eligible for reimbursement.

WINTER JOB CHECKLIST (MUST HAVE)
□ 1 pair of -70 to -100○C winter boots. CSA Approved Safety Toe and Plate (i.e., Baffin - Derrick)
TIP: -40○C Dunlop footwear does not provide sufficient insulation when temps drop below -10○C
□ Insulated coverall or bibs. See Ontario Regulations below if working in Ontario.
□ Insulated jacket. See Ontario Regulations below if working in Ontario.
□ Personal ski gloves or gauntlet gloves for travel to and from worksite
□ Long Johns
□ Neck warmer and toque or Balaclava
WINTER JOB CHECKLIST (OPTIONAL)
□ Bama Socks or Thermal Socks
□ Winter rated sleeping bag (-25○C or colder) Refer to crew change sheet for verification
TIP: A mummy bag rated for -7○C will not be adequate during extreme freezing conditions or
during a fuel shortage or power outage.

YEAR-ROUND JOB CHECKLIST (MUST HAVE)
□ 1 pair of work boots that meet the following requirements.
→ CSA approved steel toe
→ Steel Shank
→ Recommended: Leather Hiker style work boots for Heli Jobs
→ Recommended: Metatarsal protection (Internal Met Guard)
NOTE: Metatarsal Guard is required for work underground- Rubber boot style
preferred. See boot diagram below.
NOTE: Vale (Thompson) – Vale requires that all workers on site have an internal
MET Guard boot. External MET Guard will not be accepted.
□ Minimum 1 set of waterproof slickers that fit over your work gear. See Ontario Regulations
below.
NOTE: Wet rod pulls occur in the winter as well as in the summer.
□ Coveralls with reflective stripes. New employees should come prepared with one pair. Hy-Tech
will provide coveralls when your size is confirmed. See Ontario Regulations below. (NOTE: Vale
(Thompson) If you choose to not wear coveralls a Hi-Vis Shirt/Jacket and Hi-Vis Pants must
be worn.)
□ Prescription Safety Glasses if required.
APPROVED BY: FO-138 SAFETY - WORK GEAR AND PERSONAL EFFECTS (2024-01-11)
H&S MANAGER PAGE 1 / 4
SAFETY - WORK GEAR AND
PERSONAL EFFECTS FO-138
PERSONAL EFFECTS CHECKLIST (MUST HAVE)
□ Towel(s).
□ Shampoo, soap, etc.
□ Care card / Health card.
□ Major Credit Card (in case there are circumstances that would require a major credit card while
traveling to a job i.e. securing a hotel room).
□ Cash (bring an adequate cash supply in case of an emergency).
□ Prescription Drugs or Medication.
□ Medic Alert Bracelet (if you have any special medical needs).
□ Epi-pen (Epinephrine auto-injector) if you have any known severe allergies.
□ Day pack.
□ Flip flops (for community showers).
□ Water Canteens (enough drinking water for your shift).
PERSONAL EFFECTS CHECKLIST (OPTIONAL)
□ Cigarettes (if a Smoker), ensuring an adequate supply until turnaround.
□ Alarm clock.
□ Watch.
□ Leg/Calf compression socks (prevents chafing when wearing rubber boots).
□ Sunscreen in the summer.
□ Camp shoes. Refer to crew change sheet for verification or contact your scheduling
representative.
□ Sleeping bag and pillow. Refer to crew change sheet for verification or contact your
scheduling representative.

ONTARIO REGULATIONS-DUSK UNTIL DAWN AND UNDERGROUND CHECKLIST
Note: On July 1, 2016, subsection 262 (2) of the Regulation is revoked and the following
substituted (See O.Reg.265/15, s.18)
18. Subsection 262 (2) of the Regulation is revoked and the following substituted:
(2) Every worker in an underground mine shall wear,
(a) high visibility safety apparel that makes the worker visible to others in the workplace and that
meets the requirements set out in subsection (3); and
(b) retro-reflective material applied to the front, back and sides of head gear.
(3) High visibility safety apparel must meet the following requirements:
1. It shall be made of fluorescent or bright-coloured background material.
2. It shall have retro-reflective striping that,
i. is located on the outside of the garment,
ii. measures at least 50 mm in width,
iii. completely encircles the waist, each arm and each leg below the knee,
iv. is arranged in two vertical lines on the front of the garment, extending over the shoulders and
down to the waist, and
v. is arranged in the form of an “X” on the back of the garment, extending from the shoulders
and down to the waist.

Note: On July 1, 2016 subsection 263 (2) of the Regulation is revoked and the following
substituted (see O.Reg.265/15, s.19(1))
(2) Subject to subsection (3), between sunset and sunrise, every worker on the surface shall wear,
(a) high visibility safety apparel that makes the worker visible to others in the workplace and that
meets the requirements set out in subsection 262 (3); and
(b) retro-reflective material applied to the front, back and sides of head gear.
(3) A worker is not required to comply with subsection (2) if the worker is in a booth, vehicle cab or
another protective enclosure or if a worker is provided with fixed lighting that enables the worker
to be seen (see O.Reg.291/02, s.8)


Note: On July 1, 2016 subsection 263 of the Regulation is amended by adding the following
subsection (see O.Reg.265/15, s.19(2))
(4) All high visibility safety apparel and all retro-reflective material on head gear must be maintained in
good condition so that they adequately visually identify a worker.




NOTE: Hy-Tech is more than willing to support the delivery of personal effects to camp if you end up
working longer than planned, or have something unexpected come up where you need personal items
sent to you. If you arrange for a package to be delivered to any of our Hy-Tech offices, we will make sure
that you receive it.

content: None

HY - TECH DRILLING IS LOOKING FOR A FULL TIME PERMANENT FLEET
YARDPERSON TO JOIN OUR TEAM IN SASKATOON, SK.

ABOUT HY - TECH
Hy -Tech Drilling is an innovative, capable, and accountable diamond drilling partner for the leading mining
companies in the Americas and Europe , enabl ing our clients to reach critical minerals more quickly with
less environmental impact. This supports a global transition to a more sustainable future. We seek
win/win/win solutions for our people, our customers, and the communities we support.

Established in 1991, Hy -Tech has grown to a fleet of 6 0 drills operating throughout Canada, USA, Chile, and
Europe. We take pride in the success we’ve had working with our clients to develop innovative solutions
for their project challenges and believe in our team’s strength and effectiveness in tackling chal lenges that
may arise.

THE JOB
Hy -Tech is adding a Fleet Yardperson to our growing team. The Fleet Yardperson is responsible for the
efficient mobilization of work vehicles and rolling stock to meet operation needs. This position is
responsible for ensuring all work is done in accordanc e with Hy -Tech procedures and following safe work
practices. We are looking to add an ambitious, well -rounded individual to carry out the following key
responsibilities:

• Perform basic fleet maintenance, including shocks, mudflaps, tire changes, and occasional
fabrication of parts.
• Maintain a strong understanding of all mobile equipment types, their operation, and required PPE.
• Shuttle vehicles to and from repair facilities and retrieve parts as required.
• Install and wire aftermarket accessories (bumpers, lights, headache racks, etc.).
• Paint bush boxes, vehicle frames, and other add on equipment to meet Hy -Tech standards.
• Install GPS units into rolling stock, when required.
• Prepare units for disposal including thorough cleaning and removal of decals, bush boxes, and
accessories.
• Organize and ensure proper utilization of storage spaces including parts seacan, tire racks, and
fleet yard.
• Wash and detail fleet using the wash pad to ensure containment of contaminated material.
• Perform routine inspections ensuring fluid levels are topped up (i.e., fuel, DEF fluid, etc.) and all
certifications (i.e., fire extinguisher) are up to date.
• Understand and adhere to TDG, WHMIS, and transportation regulations within different regions.

THE PERKS
• Competitive wage based on experience and qualifications ($ 24.25 -$28.50 per hour) .
• Eligible for an annual performance bonus based on company performance.
• Career growth, development, and continuous learning opportunities.
• Comprehensive 100% employer -paid benefits package and progressive employer -matched RRSP
program upon successful completion of a 3 -month probationary period.
• Family access to the City of Saskatoon Leisure Centres .


THE SETTING
This position is based out of the Branch Location in Saskatoon, SK in a shop work environment. There is
also a requirement to work outside in all weather conditions. Possible exposure to dust, hazardous
chemicals, and high levels of noise.
THE SCHEDULE
Standard working hours are 7:00am – 3:30pm Monday to Friday. There will also be some requirements to
be available after hours and on weekends during busy times.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS
• Experience in a warehouse or yard position is considered an asset.
• Knowledge of basic hand tools, and experience using drill press, cutting torches, and welder
considered an asset.
• Experience operating forklifts and other heavy equipment is considered an asset.
• Basic skills in MS Office Suite.
• Ability to thrive in a challenging and fast -paced environment, juggling multiple priorities.
• Maintain high -quality standards and be a positive ambassador for Hy -Tech.
• Work independently and as part of a team, developing strong relationships.
• Perceive the bigger picture, tailoring your actions to achieve strategic objectives.
• Must have a valid driver’s licence and provide a current drivers abstract annually.



APPLICATION DEADLINE July 21, 2026

Apply online: https://hy -techdrilling.com/our -crew/job -

HY - TECH DRILLING IS LOOKING FOR A FULL TIME PERMANENT A CCOUNTS
PAYABL E CLERK TO JOIN OUR TEAM IN SMITHERS, BC OR SASKATOON, SK.

ABOUT HY - TECH
Hy -Tech Drilling is an innovative, capable, and accountable diamond drilling partner for the leading mining
companies in the Americas and Europe , enabl ing our clients to reach critical minerals more quickly with
less environmental impact. This supports a global transition to a more sustainable future. We seek
win/win/win solutions for our people, our customers, and the communities we support.

Established in 1991, Hy -Tech has grown to a fleet of 6 0 drills operating throughout Canada, USA, Chile, and
Europe. We take pride in the success we’ve had working with our clients to develop innovative solutions
for their project challenges and believe in our team’s strength and effectiveness in tackling chal lenges that
may arise.

THE JOB
This role plays an important part in supporting the financial operations of a growing international
company. The Accounts Payable Clerk is responsible for ensuring vendor payments, employee
reimbursements, and financial records are processed accurately, ef ficiently, and on time. Working closely
with employees, managers, vendors, and departments across the organization, this position is ideal for
someone who enjoys working with numbers, staying organized, and contributing to a collaborative team
environment.

We're looking for a detail -oriented professional who takes pride in accuracy and is eager to contribute to
the success of our Finance team through the following key responsibilities:
• Process accounts payable transactions accurately and efficiently in accordance with company
procedures.
• Prepare bi -weekly cheque and electronic funds transfer (EFT) payments for approved invoices and
employee reimbursements.
• Reconcile and monitor petty cash accounts and prepare related journal entries and supporting
documentation.
• Maintain employee expense accounts and ensure expenses are processed accurately and in a
timely manner.
• Assist with monthly account reconciliations and month -end financial processes.
• Audit, process, and reconcile company credit card statements.
• Maintain organized and accurate financial records in accordance with company policies and
accepted accounting practices.
• Support the development, review, and continuous improvement of company forms, procedures,
work instructions, and policies.
• Complete assigned administrative and continuous improvement initiatives in a timely manner.
• Build positive working relationships with internal departments and external vendors to support
efficient financial operations.
• Contribute to a positive team culture while maintaining a high standard of professionalism,
confidentiality, and attention to detail.

THE PERKS
• Competitive wage based on experience and qualifications ($ 25. 75 -$31.25 per hour) .
• Eligible for an annual performance bonus based on company performance.
• Career growth, development, and continuous learning opportunities.
• Comprehensive 100% employer -paid benefits package and progressive employer -matched RRSP
program upon successful completion of a 3 -month probationary period.
• Family access to :
o Bulkley Valley Pool and Recreation Centre
o City of Saskatoon Leisure Centres
THE SETTING
This position is based out of the Company Headquarters in Smithers, BC or the Branch Location in
Saskatoon, SK. Office work environment with some travel required.


THE SCHEDULE

Standard working hours are 8am – 5pm Monday to Friday. There will also be some requirements to be
available after hours and on weekends during busy times.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS
• 2–5 years of accounting, bookkeeping, or accounts payable experience.
• Post -secondary education or courses in Accounting, Bookkeeping, or a related field are considered
an asset.
• Intermediate computer skills, including experience with spreadsheets, email, databases, and word
processing software.
• Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
• Excellent organizational and time -management skills with the ability to prioritize competing
deadlines.
• Strong verbal and written communication skills.
• Ability to build positive working relationships and contribute to a team -oriented environment.
• Must have a valid driver’s licence and provide a current drivers abstract annually.



APPLICATION DEADLINE July 21, 2026

SAFETY - WORK GEAR AND
PERSONAL EFFECTS FO-138
OVERVIEW
The purpose of this document is to ensure that you are aware of your responsibility to supply work
clothing and personal effects. Hy-Tech job locations vary and so do the weather conditions and we’d like
to ensure that you are prepared for all situations.

It is important that you closely review this information prior to your departure as you are required to
supply and wear the appropriate work clothing and gear. Employees who do not have the required work
gear will be subject to Hy-Tech’s disciplinary process. Hy-Tech will work with the employee to have the
required work gear sent to the job site at the employee’s expense.

Hy-Tech will provide safety glasses, hard hat, and ear plugs. Refer to POL-02C Employee Policy; Field
(Canadian Employees) to verify other items eligible for reimbursement.

WINTER JOB CHECKLIST (MUST HAVE)
□ 1 pair of -70 to -100○C winter boots. CSA Approved Safety Toe and Plate (i.e., Baffin - Derrick)
TIP: -40○C Dunlop footwear does not provide sufficient insulation when temps drop below -10○C
□ Insulated coverall or bibs. See Ontario Regulations below if working in Ontario.
□ Insulated jacket. See Ontario Regulations below if working in Ontario.
□ Personal ski gloves or gauntlet gloves for travel to and from worksite
□ Long Johns
□ Neck warmer and toque or Balaclava
WINTER JOB CHECKLIST (OPTIONAL)
□ Bama Socks or Thermal Socks
□ Winter rated sleeping bag (-25○C or colder) Refer to crew change sheet for verification
TIP: A mummy bag rated for -7○C will not be adequate during extreme freezing conditions or
during a fuel shortage or power outage.

YEAR-ROUND JOB CHECKLIST (MUST HAVE)
□ 1 pair of work boots that meet the following requirements.
→ CSA approved steel toe
→ Steel Shank
→ Recommended: Leather Hiker style work boots for Heli Jobs
→ Recommended: Metatarsal protection (Internal Met Guard)
NOTE: Metatarsal Guard is required for work underground- Rubber boot style
preferred. See boot diagram below.
NOTE: Vale (Thompson) – Vale requires that all workers on site have an internal
MET Guard boot. External MET Guard will not be accepted.
□ Minimum 1 set of waterproof slickers that fit over your work gear. See Ontario Regulations
below.
NOTE: Wet rod pulls occur in the winter as well as in the summer.
□ Coveralls with reflective stripes. New employees should come prepared with one pair. Hy-Tech
will provide coveralls when your size is confirmed. See Ontario Regulations below. (NOTE: Vale
(Thompson) If you choose to not wear coveralls a Hi-Vis Shirt/Jacket and Hi-Vis Pants must
be worn.)
□ Prescription Safety Glasses if required.
APPROVED BY: FO-138 SAFETY - WORK GEAR AND PERSONAL EFFECTS (2024-01-11)
H&S MANAGER PAGE 1 / 4
SAFETY - WORK GEAR AND
PERSONAL EFFECTS FO-138
PERSONAL EFFECTS CHECKLIST (MUST HAVE)
□ Towel(s).
□ Shampoo, soap, etc.
□ Care card / Health card.
□ Major Credit Card (in case there are circumstances that would require a major credit card while
traveling to a job i.e. securing a hotel room).
□ Cash (bring an adequate cash supply in case of an emergency).
□ Prescription Drugs or Medication.
□ Medic Alert Bracelet (if you have any special medical needs).
□ Epi-pen (Epinephrine auto-injector) if you have any known severe allergies.
□ Day pack.
□ Flip flops (for community showers).
□ Water Canteens (enough drinking water for your shift).
PERSONAL EFFECTS CHECKLIST (OPTIONAL)
□ Cigarettes (if a Smoker), ensuring an adequate supply until turnaround.
□ Alarm clock.
□ Watch.
□ Leg/Calf compression socks (prevents chafing when wearing rubber boots).
□ Sunscreen in the summer.
□ Camp shoes. Refer to crew change sheet for verification or contact your scheduling
representative.
□ Sleeping bag and pillow. Refer to crew change sheet for verification or contact your
scheduling representative.

substituted (See O.Reg.265/15, s.18)

(2) Every worker in an underground mine shall wear,
(a) high visibility safety apparel that makes the worker visible to others in the workplace and that
meets the requirements set out in subsection (3); and
(b) retro-reflective material applied to the front, back and sides of head gear.
(3) High visibility safety apparel must meet the following requirements:
1. It shall be made of fluorescent or bright-coloured background material.
2. It shall have retro-reflective striping that,

iv. is arranged in two vertical lines on the front of the garment, extending over the shoulders and

v. is arranged in the form of an “X” on the back of the garment, extending from the shoulders
and down to the waist.

HY-TECH DRILLING IS LOOKING FOR A FULL TIME PERMANENT FIELD SCHEDULER
TO JOIN OUR TEAM IN SMITHERS, BC OR SASKATOON, SK.

ABOUT HY-TECH
Hy-Tech Drilling is an innovative, capable, and accountable diamond drilling partner for the leading mining
companies in the Americas and Europe, enabling our clients to reach critical minerals more quickly with
less environmental impact. This supports a global transition to a more sustainable future. We seek
win/win/win solutions for our people, our customers, and the communities we support.

Established in 1991, Hy-Tech has grown to a fleet of 60 drills operating throughout Canada, USA, Chile, and
Europe. We take pride in the success we’ve had working with our clients to develop innovative solutions
for their project challenges and believe in our team’s strength and effectiveness in tackling challenges that
may arise.

THE JOB
Hy-Tech is adding a Field Scheduler to our growing team. The Field Scheduler is responsible
for developing and managing crew schedules that meet operational requirements across Hy-Tech Drilling
sites. This role ensures that assignment of employees to job sites by evaluating project demands,
employee skill sets, and logistical considerations, including travel and accommodations. We are looking to
add an ambitious, well-rounded individual to carry out the following key responsibilities:
• Build relationships with employees and Foremen to understand how to best assign staff to jobs
that match their skill set, individual experience, and team requirements.
• Build a schedule to meet project needs following established procedures and client requirements.
• Attend pre-job meetings to understand job requirements and build protocols to meet client
expectations.
• Work with Contracts Manager to accommodate contract change requests by the Client.
• Work with Training to meet pre-access requirements.
• Assist the Field Scheduling Manager and HR with forecasting crew needs, ensuring an adequate
number of staff are available to meet contract requirements.
• Work with the Travel Coordinator to meet contract travel needs. Work with the Client for onsite
accommodations and travel as required.
• Review and distribute Crew Info Sheets to the drill crew, Crew Change email distribution group
and the client to ensure all parties are aware of crew movement.
• Follow Global Mobility Process when scheduling employees internationally.
• Manage last-minute staffing changes on evenings and weekends.
• Work with employees to accommodate approved time-off requests.
• Complete site-specific reports as requested by the client.
• Review candidates in progress with HR to determine suitable sites for their first rotation.
• Work with HR to help establish and work toward building a crew that meets current and future
staffing needs.
• Identify and develop relationships with high potential candidates for future opportunities
and maintain external industry ties.
• Communicate and engage with incoming employees as they complete the recruitment process,
leading up to deployment.

THE PERKS
• Competitive wage based on experience and qualifications ($37.70-$41.45 per hour).
• Eligible for an annual performance bonus based on company performance.
• Career growth, development, and continuous learning opportunities.
• Comprehensive 100% employer-paid benefits package and progressive employer-matched RRSP
program upon successful completion of a 3-month probationary period.
• Family access to:
o Bulkley Valley Pool and Recreation Centre.
o City of Saskatoon Leisure Centres.
THE SETTING
This position is based out of the Company Headquarters in Smithers, BC or the Branch Location in
Saskatoon, SK. Office work environment with some travel required.

THE SCHEDULE
Standard working hours are 8am – 5pm Monday to Friday. There will also be requirements to be available
after hours and on weekends.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS
• 2 years of experience in a scheduling or logistics focused role.
• Ability to thrive in a challenging and fast-paced environment, juggling multiple priorities.
• Maintain high-quality standards and be a positive ambassador for Hy-Tech.
• Work independently and as part of a team, developing strong relationships.
• Perceive the bigger picture, tailoring your actions to achieve strategic objectives.
• Must have a valid driver’s licence and provide a current drivers abstract annually.



APPLICATION DEADLINE May 11, 2026

Apply online: https://hy-techdrilling.com/our-crew/job-
HOW TO APPLY
opportunities/

THE JOB
This role is ideal for experienced field personnel looking to transition off the tools while remaining closely
connected to field operations.

This role involves working with the Foreman or Project Manager to oversee compliance with safety
systems and environmental regulations while providing support, guidance, and professional
representation. Responsibilities include:
• Plan and conduct site visits by developing trip plans, setting clear objectives, and completing
post‑visit reports for management.
• Work closely with Foremen to support compliance with safety systems and regulations, and
promote proactive safety practices.
• Support and participate in site safety meetings, new worker orientations, and site‑specific safety
requirements.
• Assist with the completion, review, and effective use of Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs), including
training and coaching for employees and supervisors.
• Review Hazard Identifications, incidents, and near misses; lead or support investigations, identify
root causes, and recommend corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
• Monitor legislative, industry, and internal changes to anticipate and address emerging safety
needs.
• Assist with Emergency Response Plan (ERP) development, reviews, updates, training, and annual
testing to ensure site readiness.
• Review safety meeting submissions from operations and the shop, identify trends or gaps, and
provide recommendations to the Health & Safety Manager.
• Deliver on‑site safety training as required (e.g., Propane, Defensive Driving, Rod Handler,
Lockout/Tagout).
• Conduct regular site audits to verify crews and Foremen are following company procedures and
working safely and efficiently.

THE PERKS
• Competitive wage based on experience and qualifications ($500-$600 per day).
• Eligible for an annual performance bonus based on company performance.
• Career growth, development, and continuous learning opportunities.

THE SETTING
This is a field-based position working within Canada with the potential to work on our USA job sites.

THE SCHEDULE
Rotational schedule, dependent on job location (4/2, 3/3, or 2/2).

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS
• Solid understanding of safe work practices, hazard recognition, and crew‑based job execution
gained through field experience.
• Formal safety training, diploma, or designation is considered an asset but not required — training
and support will be provided for the right candidate.
• Working knowledge (or willingness to learn) Occupational Health & Safety and environmental
requirements applicable to drilling operations across multiple jurisdictions.
• Maintain high-quality standards and be a positive ambassador for Hy-Tech.
• Work independently and as part of a team, developing strong relationships.
• Must have a valid driver’s licence and provide a current drivers abstract annually.

HY - TECH DRILLING IS LOOKING FOR A FULL TIME PERMANENT FLEET
YARDPERSON TO JOIN OUR TEAM IN SASKATOON, SK.

ABOUT HY - TECH
Hy -Tech Drilling is an innovative, capable, and accountable diamond drilling partner for the leading mining
companies in the Americas and Europe , enabl ing our clients to reach critical minerals more quickly with
less environmental impact. This supports a global transition to a more sustainable future. We seek
win/win/win solutions for our people, our customers, and the communities we support.

Established in 1991, Hy -Tech has grown to a fleet of 6 0 drills operating throughout Canada, USA, Chile, and
Europe. We take pride in the success we’ve had working with our clients to develop innovative solutions
for their project challenges and believe in our team’s strength and effectiveness in tackling chal lenges that
may arise.

THE JOB
Hy -Tech is adding a Fleet Yardperson to our growing team. The Fleet Yardperson is responsible for the
efficient mobilization of work vehicles and rolling stock to meet operation needs. This position is
responsible for ensuring all work is done in accordanc e with Hy -Tech procedures and following safe work
practices. We are looking to add an ambitious, well -rounded individual to carry out the following key
responsibilities:

• Perform basic fleet maintenance, including shocks, mudflaps, tire changes, and occasional
fabrication of parts.
• Maintain a strong understanding of all mobile equipment types, their operation, and required PPE.
• Shuttle vehicles to and from repair facilities and retrieve parts as required.
• Install and wire aftermarket accessories (bumpers, lights, headache racks, etc.).
• Paint bush boxes, vehicle frames, and other add on equipment to meet Hy -Tech standards.
• Install GPS units into rolling stock, when required.
• Prepare units for disposal including thorough cleaning and removal of decals, bush boxes, and
accessories.
• Organize and ensure proper utilization of storage spaces including parts seacan, tire racks, and
fleet yard.
• Wash and detail fleet using the wash pad to ensure containment of contaminated material.
• Perform routine inspections ensuring fluid levels are topped up (i.e., fuel, DEF fluid, etc.) and all
certifications (i.e., fire extinguisher) are up to date.
• Understand and adhere to TDG, WHMIS, and transportation regulations within different regions.

THE PERKS
• Competitive wage based on experience and qualifications ($ 24.25 -$28.50 per hour) .
• Eligible for an annual performance bonus based on company performance.
• Career growth, development, and continuous learning opportunities.
• Comprehensive 100% employer -paid benefits package and progressive employer -matched RRSP
program upon successful completion of a 3 -month probationary period.
• Family access to the City of Saskatoon Leisure Centres .


THE SETTING
This position is based out of the Branch Location in Saskatoon, SK in a shop work environment. There is
also a requirement to work outside in all weather conditions. Possible exposure to dust, hazardous
chemicals, and high levels of noise.
THE SCHEDULE
Standard working hours are 7:00am – 3:30pm Monday to Friday. There will also be some requirements to
be available after hours and on weekends during busy times.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS
• Experience in a warehouse or yard position is considered an asset.
• Knowledge of basic hand tools, and experience using drill press, cutting torches, and welder
considered an asset.
• Experience operating forklifts and other heavy equipment is considered an asset.
• Basic skills in MS Office Suite.
• Ability to thrive in a challenging and fast -paced environment, juggling multiple priorities.
• Maintain high -quality standards and be a positive ambassador for Hy -Tech.
• Work independently and as part of a team, developing strong relationships.
• Perceive the bigger picture, tailoring your actions to achieve strategic objectives.
• Must have a valid driver’s licence and provide a current drivers abstract annually.

company. The Accounts Payable Clerk is responsible for ensuring vendor payments, employee
reimbursements, and financial records are processed accurately, ef ficiently, and on time. Working closely
with employees, managers, vendors, and departments across the organization, this position is ideal for
someone who enjoys working with numbers, staying organized, and contributing to a collaborative team

the success of our Finance team through the following key responsibilities:
• Process accounts payable transactions accurately and efficiently in accordance with company
procedures.
• Prepare bi -weekly cheque and electronic funds transfer (EFT) payments for approved invoices and
employee reimbursements.
• Reconcile and monitor petty cash accounts and prepare related journal entries and supporting
documentation.
• Maintain employee expense accounts and ensure expenses are processed accurately and in a
timely manner.
• Assist with monthly account reconciliations and month -end financial processes.
• Audit, process, and reconcile company credit card statements.
• Maintain organized and accurate financial records in accordance with company policies and
accepted accounting practices.
• Support the development, review, and continuous improvement of company forms, procedures,
work instructions, and policies.
• Complete assigned administrative and continuous improvement initiatives in a timely manner.
• Build positive working relationships with internal departments and external vendors to support
efficient financial operations.
• Contribute to a positive team culture while maintaining a high standard of professionalism,
confidentiality, and attention to detail.

• Competitive wage based on experience and qualifications ($ 25. 75 -$31.25 per hour) .
• Eligible for an annual performance bonus based on company performance.
• Career growth, development, and continuous learning opportunities.
• Comprehensive 100% employer -paid benefits package and progressive employer -matched RRSP
program upon successful completion of a 3 -month probationary period.
• Family access to :
o Bulkley Valley Pool and Recreation Centre
o City of Saskatoon Leisure Centres
THE SETTING
This position is based out of the Company Headquarters in Smithers, BC or the Branch Location in
Saskatoon, SK. Office work environment with some travel required.


THE SCHEDULE

Standard working hours are 8am – 5pm Monday to Friday. There will also be some requirements to be
available after hours and on weekends during busy times.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS
• 2–5 years of accounting, bookkeeping, or accounts payable experience.
• Post -secondary education or courses in Accounting, Bookkeeping, or a related field are considered
an asset.
• Intermediate computer skills, including experience with spreadsheets, email, databases, and word
processing software.
• Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
• Excellent organizational and time -management skills with the ability to prioritize competing
deadlines.
• Strong verbal and written communication skills.
• Ability to build positive working relationships and contribute to a team -oriented environment.
• Must have a valid driver’s licence and provide a current drivers abstract annually.

The Montreal Convention or the Warsaw Convention system may be applicable to your journey and these Conventions govern and
may limit the liability of air carriers for death or bodily injury, for loss of or damage to baggage, and for delay.

Where the Montreal Convention applies, the limits of liability are as follows:

1. There are no financial limits in respect of death or bodily injury.

SAFETY - WORK GEAR AND
PERSONAL EFFECTS FO-138
OVERVIEW
The purpose of this document is to ensure that you are aware of your responsibility to supply work
clothing and personal effects. Hy-Tech job locations vary and so do the weather conditions and we’d like
to ensure that you are prepared for all situations.

It is important that you closely review this information prior to your departure as you are required to
supply and wear the appropriate work clothing and gear. Employees who do not have the required work
gear will be subject to Hy-Tech’s disciplinary process. Hy-Tech will work with the employee to have the
required work gear sent to the job site at the employee’s expense.

Hy-Tech will provide safety glasses, hard hat, and ear plugs. Refer to POL-02C Employee Policy; Field
(Canadian Employees) to verify other items eligible for reimbursement.

WINTER JOB CHECKLIST (MUST HAVE)
□ 1 pair of -70 to -100○C winter boots. CSA Approved Safety Toe and Plate (i.e., Baffin - Derrick)
TIP: -40○C Dunlop footwear does not provide sufficient insulation when temps drop below -10○C
□ Insulated coverall or bibs. See Ontario Regulations below if working in Ontario.
□ Insulated jacket. See Ontario Regulations below if working in Ontario.
□ Personal ski gloves or gauntlet gloves for travel to and from worksite
□ Long Johns
□ Neck warmer and toque or Balaclava
WINTER JOB CHECKLIST (OPTIONAL)
□ Bama Socks or Thermal Socks
□ Winter rated sleeping bag (-25○C or colder) Refer to crew change sheet for verification
TIP: A mummy bag rated for -7○C will not be adequate during extreme freezing conditions or
during a fuel shortage or power outage.

YEAR-ROUND JOB CHECKLIST (MUST HAVE)
□ 1 pair of work boots that meet the following requirements.
→ CSA approved steel toe
→ Steel Shank
→ Recommended: Leather Hiker style work boots for Heli Jobs
→ Recommended: Metatarsal protection (Internal Met Guard)
NOTE: Metatarsal Guard is required for work underground- Rubber boot style
preferred. See boot diagram below.
NOTE: Vale (Thompson) – Vale requires that all workers on site have an internal
MET Guard boot. External MET Guard will not be accepted.
□ Minimum 1 set of waterproof slickers that fit over your work gear. See Ontario Regulations
below.
NOTE: Wet rod pulls occur in the winter as well as in the summer.
□ Coveralls with reflective stripes. New employees should come prepared with one pair. Hy-Tech
will provide coveralls when your size is confirmed. See Ontario Regulations below. (NOTE: Vale
(Thompson) If you choose to not wear coveralls a Hi-Vis Shirt/Jacket and Hi-Vis Pants must
be worn.)
□ Prescription Safety Glasses if required.

SAFETY - WORK GEAR AND
PERSONAL EFFECTS FO-138
PERSONAL EFFECTS CHECKLIST (MUST HAVE)
□ Towel(s).
□ Shampoo, soap, etc.
□ Care card / Health card.
□ Major Credit Card (in case there are circumstances that would require a major credit card while
traveling to a job i.e. securing a hotel room).
□ Cash (bring an adequate cash supply in case of an emergency).
□ Prescription Drugs or Medication.
□ Medic Alert Bracelet (if you have any special medical needs).
□ Epi-pen (Epinephrine auto-injector) if you have any known severe allergies.
□ Day pack.
□ Flip flops (for community showers).
□ Water Canteens (enough drinking water for your shift).
PERSONAL EFFECTS CHECKLIST (OPTIONAL)
□ Cigarettes (if a Smoker), ensuring an adequate supply until turnaround.
□ Alarm clock.
□ Watch.
□ Leg/Calf compression socks (prevents chafing when wearing rubber boots).
□ Sunscreen in the summer.
□ Camp shoes. Refer to crew change sheet for verification or contact your scheduling
representative.
□ Sleeping bag and pillow. Refer to crew change sheet for verification or contact your
scheduling representative.

2. Although reconfirmation of flights is not required, we strongly recommend that you check your flight status online at
aircanada.com or by calling our flight information system at 1-888-422-7533 prior to your departure.

3. Advance seat assignments are not guaranteed and may change without notice. If your pre-assigned seat is unavailable, we
will try to accommodate you in a
comparable seat in the same class of service and will refund any applicable fees.

4. Any travel credit banked for unused tickets is non-transferable: when the credit is redeemed, it must be used by the same
person whose name appears on the original ticket.

5. Air Canada will cancel any purchased ticket and provide a full refund without penalty up to 24 hours after purchase. Beyond 24
hours, voluntary changes to your itinerary may require the payment of additional fees and fare upgrades. If you are travelling
on a non-refundable ticket, Air Canada will be unable to make exceptions in the event of an unexpected trip cancellation or
medical emergency. We recommend the purchase of travel insurance.

6. Dangerous goods

For safety reasons, dangerous goods must not be packed in checked or carry-on baggage, except as specifically permitted.
Dangerous goods include, but are not limited to: compressed gases, corrosives, explosives, flammable liquids and solids,
radioactive materials, oxidizing materials, poisons, infectious substances, and briefcases with installed alarm devices. For
security reasons, other restrictions may apply. Please refer to the Restricted and Prohibited Items page on our website for
more information.

7. Subject to the provisions of the Montreal Convention and the Warsaw Convention, as well as the provisions of its applicable
tariffs, Air Canada may refuse carriage of property in checked luggage that is not suitable for transportation, such as fragile or
perishable items and may refuse to carry valuable items (a valuable is deemed to be any item whose value is $ 1,000 CAD or
more, per Kilogram or $1 CAD per gram). Air Canada may refuse claims based on the inherent nature of an item (e.g. its
perishable nature), or for loss or delay of unsuitably or inadequately packed items, to the extent that the destruction, loss or
damages resulted from the inherent defect, quality or vice of the baggage, or, in the case of delay, that the carrier, its agents,
and servants took all measures that could reasonably be required to avoid the damage, or that it was impossible to take such
measures.

8. International travel

Governments may require your carrier to provide information on or permit access to passenger data. You cannot travel if you
do not have all required travel documents, such as a passport and visa (where applicable), to enter in or transit through each
country on your itinerary. Please refer to the Travel Documents page on our website for more information.

9. In-flight health

Most people are fit to travel by air, but special attention is required for passengers whose health problems may be exacerbated
by altitude, travel stress, hypoxia and other travel related difficulties. Our website offers important health tips and information
for customers with special needs who may require medical approval before flying. Please also note that aircraft disinsection is
carried out on certain routes, in compliance with the requirements of the World Health Organization (WHO), the International
Civil Aviation Organization, Transport Canada and applicable foreign regulatory authorities. More information is available on
our website.

10. Schedules and timetables

Time and aircraft type shown in timetables or elsewhere are approximate and not guaranteed, and form no part of the contract.
Schedules are subject to change without notice and carrier assumes no responsibility for passenger making connections not
included as part of the itinerary set out in the ticket. Carrier is not responsible for changes, errors or omissions either in
timetables or other representations of schedules.

11. Overbooking notice

Airline flights may be overbooked, and there is a slight chance that a seat will not be available on a flight for which a person
has a confirmed reservation. If the flight is overbooked, no one will be denied a seat until airline personnel first ask for
volunteers willing to give up their reservation in exchange for a payment of the airline's choosing. If there are not enough
volunteers, the airline will deny boarding to other persons in accordance with its particular boarding priority. With few
exceptions, persons denied boarding involuntarily are entitled to compensation. The complete rules for the payment of
compensation and boarding priorities are available at all airport ticket counters and boarding locations.


NOTICE: SOLD SUBJECT TO APPLICABLE TARIFFS
Schedule and Itinerary Changes

Please contact the Air Canada Contact Centre immediately if you have any questions concerning any schedule change.
Any changes made to Air Canada bookings may affect other travel services you may have booked/reserved (i.e. car and/or
hotel reservations). It is your responsibility to verify whether or not other travel services are affected as a result of such
changes.
If the flight for which you have a confirmed upgrade has been cancelled and we were not able to rebook you in the Business
Class cabin, any eUpgrade Credits or frequent flyer miles/points that were used for the initial upgrade will be returned to your
account.
You can change your new seat assignment on aircanada.com. If you wish to change your new flight, please contact the Air
Canada Contact Centre.


CONDITIONS OF CONTRACT AND OTHER IMPORTANT NOTICES

PASSENGERS ON A JOURNEY INVOLVING AN ULTIMATE DESTINATION OR A STOP IN A COUNTRY OTHER THAN THE
COUNTRY OF DEPARTURE ARE ADVISED THAT INTERNATIONAL TREATIES KNOWN AS THE MONTREAL CONVENTION, OR
ITS PREDECESSOR, THE WARSAW CONVENTION, INCLUDING ITS AMENDMENTS (THE WARSAW CONVENTION SYSTEM),
MAY APPLY TO THE ENTIRE JOURNEY, INCLUDING ANY PORTION THEREOF WITHIN A COUNTRY. FOR SUCH
PASSENGERS, THE APPLICABLE TREATY, INCLUDING SPECIAL CONTRACTS OF CARRIAGE EMBODIED IN ANY APPLICABLE
TARIFFS, GOVERNS AND MAY LIMIT THE LIABILITY OF THE CARRIER.

Air Passenger Protection Regulations Notice (for flights to, from and within Canada, including connecting flights):

If you are denied boarding, your flight is cancelled or delayed for at least two hours, or your baggage is lost or damaged, you may be
entitled to certain standards of treatment and compensation under the Air Passenger Protection Regulations . For more information
about your passenger rights please contact your air carrier or visit the Canadian Transportation Agency’s website.

Pursuant to these regulations, general terms and conditions pertaining to flight delays, cancellations, denied boarding, seating of
children and lost or damaged baggage must be provided by your carrier. For Air Canada, this information can be found in Air Canadas
General Conditions of Carriage and Tariffs.

Air Canada applies travel document and animal entry and exit requirements contained in IATA’s Travel Information Manual, available
on the IATA Travel Centre website.


NOTICE of Liability Limitations

The Montreal Convention or the Warsaw Convention system may be applicable to your journey and these Conventions govern and
may limit the liability of air carriers for death or bodily injury, for loss of or damage to baggage, and for delay.

Where the Montreal Convention applies, the limits of liability are as follows:

1. There are no financial limits in respect of death or bodily injury.
2. In respect of destruction, loss of, or damage or delay to baggage, 1,519 Special Drawing Rights (approximately $2,800 CAD)
per passenger in most cases.
3. For damage occasioned by delay to your journey, 6,303 Special Drawing Rights (approximately $11,000 CAD) per passenger
in most cases.

Where the Warsaw Convention system applies, the following limits of liability may apply:

1. 16,600 Special Drawing Rights (approximately EUR 20,000; US $20,000) in respect of death or bodily injury if the Hague
Protocol to the Convention applies, or 8,300 Special Drawing Rights (approximately EUR 10,000; US $10,000) if only the
Warsaw Convention applies. Many carriers have voluntarily waived these limits in their entirety, and US regulations require
that, for journeys to, from or with an agreed stopping place in the US, the limit may not be less than US $75,000.
2. 17 Special Drawing Rights (approximately EUR 20; US $20) per kg for loss of or damage or delay to checked baggage and
332 Special Drawing Rights (approximately EUR 400; US $400) for unchecked baggage.
3. The carrier may also be liable for damage occasioned by delay.

Air Canada waives its limits of liability for lost, damaged and delayed mobility aids, when such items have been accepted as checked
baggage. For more information, please consult our website and our tariffs.

Where neither the Montreal Convention nor the Warsaw Convention system applies: For travel wholly between points in Canada, the
liability limit for loss or delay of, or damage to baggage is 1,519 Special Drawing Rights (approximately $2,800 CAD) per passenger.

Further information may be obtained from Air Canada as to the limits applicable to your journey. If your journey involves carriage by
different carriers, you should contact each carrier for information on the applicable limits of liability.

Regardless of which Convention applies to your journey, you may benefit from a higher limit of liability for loss of, damage or delay to
baggage by making at check-in a special declaration of the value of your baggage and paying any supplementary fee that may apply.
Alternatively, if the value of your baggage exceeds the applicable limit of liability, you should fully insure it before you travel.

Time limit for action: Any action in court to claim damages must be brought within two years from the date of arrival of the aircraft, or
from the date on which the aircraft ought to have arrived. Baggage claims: Written notice to the carrier must be made within 7 days of
the receipt of checked baggage in the case of damage, and, in the case of delay, within 21 days from the date on which it was
placed at the disposal of the passenger.


Notice of Contract Terms Incorporated by Reference

1. Your contract of carriage with the carrier that provides you with carriage by air, whether international, domestic or a domestic
portion of an international journey is subject to this notice; to any notice or receipt of the carrier; and to the carriers individual
terms and conditions (Conditions), related rules, regulations and policies (Regulations) and any applicable tariffs.
2. If your carriage is by more than one carrier, different Conditions, Regulations and any applicable tariffs may apply for each
carrier.
3. The Conditions, Regulations and any applicable tariffs of each carrier are, by this notice, incorporated by reference into and
made part of your contract of carriage.
4. The Conditions may include, but are not restricted to:
Conditions and limits on the carriers liability for the bodily injury or death of passengers.
Conditions and limits on the carriers liability for the loss of, damage to or delay of goods and baggage, including fragile
or perishable goods.
Rules for declaring a higher value for baggage and for paying any supplementary fee that may apply.
Application of the carriers Conditions and limits of liability to the acts of the carriers agents, servants and
representatives, including any person providing either equipment or services to the carrier.
Claims restrictions, including time limits by which passengers must file claims or bring actions against the carrier.
Rules about reconfirmations or reservations; check in times; the use, duration and validity of air transportation services;
and the carriers right to refuse carriage.
Rights of the carrier and limits on the carriers liability for delay or failure to perform a service, including schedule
changes, substitution of alternative carriers or aircraft and re-routing, and, when required by applicable law, the
obligation of the carrier to notify passengers of the identity of the operating carrier or substituted aircraft.
Rights of the carrier to refuse carriage to passengers who fail to comply with applicable laws or who fail to present all
necessary travel documents.
5. You can obtain more information about your contract of carriage, and find out how to request a copy, at places where
transportation on the carrier is sold. Many carriers also have this information on their websites. When required by applicable
law, you have the right to inspect the full text of your contract of carriage at the carriers airport and sales offices, and upon
request, to receive a copy by mail or other delivery service from each carrier free of charge.
6. If a carrier sells air transportation services or checks baggage specifying carriage on another carrier, it does so only as agent
for the other carrier.


China departing flights only

1. Passenger notifications

In the event that a flight is delayed, cancelled or diverted due to an unforeseen problem, we will make every effort to keep you
well informed at the airport and onboard the affected aircraft. Based on the information we have, we will promptly provide
timely updates, within 30 minutes of becoming aware of such a cancellation, delay or diversion, and explain the reason for the
delay, cancellation or diversion through various methods, such as:
onboard/gate announcements
our Flight Status tool on our website
the airport Flight Information Display Systems
calling Air Canada Reservations

You may also register for our Flight Notification Service to receive delay or cancellation information or gate change
details for your flight.

2. Flight delays and cancellations

If you are affected by a situation that causes a delay or flight cancellation, we provide the details of how Air Canada will assist
you.
3. Response plan for Tarmac Delays

Our contingency plan for lengthy tarmac delays at Chinese airports is intended to provide you with information regarding Air
Canadas policies and procedures for handling your travel on our airline in the event of a lengthy ground delay, while you are
onboard our aircraft at a Chinese airport.

HY-TECH DRILLING IS LOOKING FOR A FULL TIME PERMANENT FIELD SCHEDULER
TO JOIN OUR TEAM IN SMITHERS, BC OR SASKATOON, SK.

ABOUT HY-TECH
Hy-Tech Drilling is an innovative, capable, and accountable diamond drilling partner for the leading mining
companies in the Americas and Europe, enabling our clients to reach critical minerals more quickly with
less environmental impact. This supports a global transition to a more sustainable future. We seek
win/win/win solutions for our people, our customers, and the communities we support.

Established in 1991, Hy-Tech has grown to a fleet of 60 drills operating throughout Canada, USA, Chile, and
Europe. We take pride in the success we’ve had working with our clients to develop innovative solutions
for their project challenges and believe in our team’s strength and effectiveness in tackling challenges that
may arise.

THE JOB
Hy-Tech is adding a Field Scheduler to our growing team. The Field Scheduler is responsible
for developing and managing crew schedules that meet operational requirements across Hy-Tech Drilling
sites. This role ensures that assignment of employees to job sites by evaluating project demands,
employee skill sets, and logistical considerations, including travel and accommodations. We are looking to
add an ambitious, well-rounded individual to carry out the following key responsibilities:
• Build relationships with employees and Foremen to understand how to best assign staff to jobs
that match their skill set, individual experience, and team requirements.
• Build a schedule to meet project needs following established procedures and client requirements.
• Attend pre-job meetings to understand job requirements and build protocols to meet client
expectations.
• Work with Contracts Manager to accommodate contract change requests by the Client.
• Work with Training to meet pre-access requirements.
• Assist the Field Scheduling Manager and HR with forecasting crew needs, ensuring an adequate
number of staff are available to meet contract requirements.
• Work with the Travel Coordinator to meet contract travel needs. Work with the Client for onsite
accommodations and travel as required.
• Review and distribute Crew Info Sheets to the drill crew, Crew Change email distribution group
and the client to ensure all parties are aware of crew movement.
• Follow Global Mobility Process when scheduling employees internationally.
• Manage last-minute staffing changes on evenings and weekends.
• Work with employees to accommodate approved time-off requests.
• Complete site-specific reports as requested by the client.
• Review candidates in progress with HR to determine suitable sites for their first rotation.
• Work with HR to help establish and work toward building a crew that meets current and future
staffing needs.
• Identify and develop relationships with high potential candidates for future opportunities
and maintain external industry ties.
• Communicate and engage with incoming employees as they complete the recruitment process,
leading up to deployment.

THE PERKS
• Competitive wage based on experience and qualifications ($37.70-$41.45 per hour).
• Eligible for an annual performance bonus based on company performance.
• Career growth, development, and continuous learning opportunities.
• Comprehensive 100% employer-paid benefits package and progressive employer-matched RRSP
program upon successful completion of a 3-month probationary period.
• Family access to:
o Bulkley Valley Pool and Recreation Centre.
o City of Saskatoon Leisure Centres.
THE SETTING
This position is based out of the Company Headquarters in Smithers, BC or the Branch Location in
Saskatoon, SK. Office work environment with some travel required.

THE SCHEDULE
Standard working hours are 8am – 5pm Monday to Friday. There will also be requirements to be available
after hours and on weekends.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS
• 2 years of experience in a scheduling or logistics focused role.
• Ability to thrive in a challenging and fast-paced environment, juggling multiple priorities.
• Maintain high-quality standards and be a positive ambassador for Hy-Tech.
• Work independently and as part of a team, developing strong relationships.
• Perceive the bigger picture, tailoring your actions to achieve strategic objectives.
• Must have a valid driver’s licence and provide a current drivers abstract annually.

HY-TECH DRILLING IS LOOKING FOR A FULL TIME PERMANENT FIELD SAFETY
COORDINATOR TO JOIN OUR TEAM.

THE JOB
This role is ideal for experienced field personnel looking to transition off the tools while remaining closely
connected to field operations.

This role involves working with the Foreman or Project Manager to oversee compliance with safety
systems and environmental regulations while providing support, guidance, and professional
representation. Responsibilities include:
• Plan and conduct site visits by developing trip plans, setting clear objectives, and completing
post‑visit reports for management.
• Work closely with Foremen to support compliance with safety systems and regulations, and
promote proactive safety practices.
• Support and participate in site safety meetings, new worker orientations, and site‑specific safety
requirements.
• Assist with the completion, review, and effective use of Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs), including
training and coaching for employees and supervisors.
• Review Hazard Identifications, incidents, and near misses; lead or support investigations, identify
root causes, and recommend corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
• Monitor legislative, industry, and internal changes to anticipate and address emerging safety
needs.
• Assist with Emergency Response Plan (ERP) development, reviews, updates, training, and annual
testing to ensure site readiness.
• Review safety meeting submissions from operations and the shop, identify trends or gaps, and
provide recommendations to the Health & Safety Manager.
• Deliver on‑site safety training as required (e.g., Propane, Defensive Driving, Rod Handler,
Lockout/Tagout).
• Conduct regular site audits to verify crews and Foremen are following company procedures and
working safely and efficiently.

THE PERKS
• Competitive wage based on experience and qualifications ($500-$600 per day).
• Eligible for an annual performance bonus based on company performance.
• Career growth, development, and continuous learning opportunities.

THE SETTING
This is a field-based position working within Canada with the potential to work on our USA job sites.

THE SCHEDULE
Rotational schedule, dependent on job location (4/2, 3/3, or 2/2).

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS
• Solid understanding of safe work practices, hazard recognition, and crew‑based job execution
gained through field experience.
• Formal safety training, diploma, or designation is considered an asset but not required — training
and support will be provided for the right candidate.
• Working knowledge (or willingness to learn) Occupational Health & Safety and environmental
requirements applicable to drilling operations across multiple jurisdictions.
• Maintain high-quality standards and be a positive ambassador for Hy-Tech.
• Work independently and as part of a team, developing strong relationships.
• Must have a valid driver’s licence and provide a current drivers abstract annually.
APPLICATION DEADLINE May 5, 2026

HOW TO APPLY Email HR@hy-techdrilling.com


FOR MORE INFORMATION Contact Matt: (236) 259-6349

SAFETY - WORK GEAR AND
PERSONAL EFFECTS FO-138
OVERVIEW
The purpose of this document is to ensure that you are aware of your responsibility to supply work
clothing and personal effects. Hy-Tech job locations vary and so do the weather conditions and we’d like
to ensure that you are prepared for all situations.

It is important that you closely review this information prior to your departure as you are required to
supply and wear the appropriate work clothing and gear. Employees who do not have the required work
gear will be subject to Hy-Tech’s disciplinary process. Hy-Tech will work with the employee to have the
required work gear sent to the job site at the employee’s expense.

Hy-Tech will provide safety glasses, hard hat, and ear plugs. Refer to POL-02C Employee Policy; Field
(Canadian Employees) to verify other items eligible for reimbursement.

WINTER JOB CHECKLIST (MUST HAVE)
□ 1 pair of -70 to -100○C winter boots. CSA Approved Safety Toe and Plate (i.e., Baffin - Derrick)
TIP: -40○C Dunlop footwear does not provide sufficient insulation when temps drop below -10○C
□ Insulated coverall or bibs. See Ontario Regulations below if working in Ontario.
□ Insulated jacket. See Ontario Regulations below if working in Ontario.
□ Personal ski gloves or gauntlet gloves for travel to and from worksite
□ Long Johns
□ Neck warmer and toque or Balaclava
WINTER JOB CHECKLIST (OPTIONAL)
□ Bama Socks or Thermal Socks
□ Winter rated sleeping bag (-25○C or colder) Refer to crew change sheet for verification
TIP: A mummy bag rated for -7○C will not be adequate during extreme freezing conditions or
during a fuel shortage or power outage.

YEAR-ROUND JOB CHECKLIST (MUST HAVE)
□ 1 pair of work boots that meet the following requirements.
→ CSA approved steel toe
→ Steel Shank
→ Recommended: Leather Hiker style work boots for Heli Jobs
→ Recommended: Metatarsal protection (Internal Met Guard)
NOTE: Metatarsal Guard is required for work underground- Rubber boot style
preferred. See boot diagram below.

content: None

HY-TECH DRILLING IS LOOKING FOR A FULL TIME PERMANENT FLEET
COORDINATOR TO JOIN OUR TEAM IN SMITHERS, BC.

ABOUT HY-TECH
Hy-Tech Drilling is an innovative, capable, and accountable diamond drilling partner for the leading mining
companies in the Americas and Europe, enabling our clients to reach critical minerals more quickly with
less environmental impact. This supports a global transition to a more sustainable future. We seek
win/win/win solutions for our people, our customers, and the communities we support.

Established in 1991, Hy-Tech has grown to a fleet of 60 drills operating throughout Canada, USA, Chile, and
Europe. We take pride in the success we’ve had working with our clients to develop innovative solutions
for their project challenges and believe in our team’s strength and effectiveness in tackling challenges that
may arise.

THE JOB
Hy-Tech is adding a Fleet Coordinator to our growing team. The Fleet Coordinator is responsible for
planning, scheduling and coordinating all required repairs and maintenance associated with the
company’s fleet of rolling stock. This role involves assisting with the mobilization and demobilization of
equipment to and from the field. We are looking to add an ambitious, well-rounded individual to carry out
the following key responsibilities:

• Coordinate fleet to ensure rolling stock is in good condition and schedule required services and
maintenance.
• Assist with developing and updating the preventative maintenance program for the company fleet.
• Monitor GPS units to ensure proper operation.
• Collaborate with Fleet System Coordinator to maintain Fleetio, recording all rolling stock
inspections, maintenance, and repair history.
• Collaborate with Fleet Manager to purchase inventory requirements for to support fleet repair and
maintenance.
• Ensure the company’s fleet requirements for applicable certificates and licenses are in place.
• Ensure correct fleet insurance and registration are in vehicles.
• Maintain current knowledge and awareness of safety and DOT regulations in all jurisdictions.
• Collaborate with the Fleet Manager to ensure vehicle and equipment needs are met prior to project
mobilization.
• Collaborate with Scheduling to ensure crew change requirements are met.
• Work closely with Logistics to have vehicles available for crew changes.
• Assist with the development of Mobilization Lists based on contract requirements.

THE PERKS
• Competitive wage based on experience and qualifications ($23.50-$33.25 per hour).
• Eligible for an annual performance bonus based on company performance.
• Career growth, development, and continuous learning opportunities.
• Comprehensive 100% employer-paid benefits package and progressive employer-matched RRSP
program upon successful completion of a 3-month probationary period.
• Family access to Bulkley Valley Pool and Recreation Centre.


THE SETTING
This position is based out of the Company Headquarters in Smithers, BC. Shop work environment. There
is also a requirement to work outside in all weather conditions. Possible exposure to dust, hazardous
chemicals, and high levels of noise.
THE SCHEDULE
Standard working hours are 8:00am – 4:30pm Monday to Friday. There will also be some requirements to
be available after hours and on weekends during busy times.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS
• 2+ years of Fleet Management/Coordinator experience in a related industry.
• Red Seal Certification in relevant trade is considered an asset.
• Knowledge of diamond drill equipment and drilling methodologies is an asset.
• Knowledge of fleet related regulations in relevant jurisdictions is considered an asset.
• Experience with fleet management software is considered an asset.
• Ability to thrive in a challenging and fast-paced environment, juggling multiple priorities.
• Maintain high-quality standards and be a positive ambassador for Hy-Tech.
• Work independently and as part of a team, developing strong relationships.
• Perceive the bigger picture, tailoring your actions to achieve strategic objectives.
• Must have a valid driver’s licence and provide a current drivers abstract annually.



APPLICATION DEADLINE September 24, 2026

Apply online: https://hy-techdrilling.com/our-crew/job-
HOW TO APPLY opportunities/

6. Dangerous goods

For safety reasons, dangerous goods must not be packed in checked or carry-on baggage, except as specifically permitted.

ITS PREDECESSOR, THE WARSAW CONVENTION, INCLUDING ITS AMENDMENTS (THE WARSAW CONVENTION SYSTEM),

Air Passenger Protection Regulations Notice (for flights to, from and within Canada, including connecting flights):

If you are denied boarding, your flight is cancelled or delayed for at least two hours, or your baggage is lost or damaged, you may be

NOTICE of Liability Limitations

The Montreal Convention or the Warsaw Convention system may be applicable to your journey and these Conventions govern and
may limit the liability of air carriers for death or bodily injury, for loss of or damage to baggage, and for delay.

Where the Montreal Convention applies, the limits of liability are as follows:

1. There are no financial limits in respect of death or bodily injury.
2. In respect of destruction, loss of, or damage or delay to baggage, 1,519 Special Drawing Rights (approximately $2,800 CAD)
per passenger in most cases.
3. For damage occasioned by delay to your journey, 6,303 Special Drawing Rights (approximately $11,000 CAD) per passenger
in most cases.

Where the Warsaw Convention system applies, the following limits of liability may apply:

1. 16,600 Special Drawing Rights (approximately EUR 20,000; US $20,000) in respect of death or bodily injury if the Hague
Protocol to the Convention applies, or 8,300 Special Drawing Rights (approximately EUR 10,000; US $10,000) if only the
Warsaw Convention applies. Many carriers have voluntarily waived these limits in their entirety, and US regulations require
that, for journeys to, from or with an agreed stopping place in the US, the limit may not be less than US $75,000.
2. 17 Special Drawing Rights (approximately EUR 20; US $20) per kg for loss of or damage or delay to checked baggage and

3. The carrier may also be liable for damage occasioned by delay.

Air Canada waives its limits of liability for lost, damaged and delayed mobility aids, when such items have been accepted as checked

Where neither the Montreal Convention nor the Warsaw Convention system applies: For travel wholly between points in Canada, the

Further information may be obtained from Air Canada as to the limits applicable to your journey. If your journey involves carriage by
different carriers, you should contact each carrier for information on the applicable limits of liability.

Regardless of which Convention applies to your journey, you may benefit from a higher limit of liability for loss of, damage or delay to
baggage by making at check-in a special declaration of the value of your baggage and paying any supplementary fee that may apply.
Alternatively, if the value of your baggage exceeds the applicable limit of liability, you should fully insure it before you travel.

Time limit for action: Any action in court to claim damages must be brought within two years from the date of arrival of the aircraft, or

SAFETY - WORK GEAR AND
PERSONAL EFFECTS FO-138
OVERVIEW
The purpose of this document is to ensure that you are aware of your responsibility to supply work
clothing and personal effects. Hy-Tech job locations vary and so do the weather conditions and we’d like
to ensure that you are prepared for all situations.

It is important that you closely review this information prior to your departure as you are required to
supply and wear the appropriate work clothing and gear. Employees who do not have the required work
gear will be subject to Hy-Tech’s disciplinary process. Hy-Tech will work with the employee to have the
required work gear sent to the job site at the employee’s expense.

Hy-Tech will provide safety glasses, hard hat, and ear plugs. Refer to POL-02C Employee Policy; Field
(Canadian Employees) to verify other items eligible for reimbursement.

WINTER JOB CHECKLIST (MUST HAVE)
□ 1 pair of -70 to -100○C winter boots. CSA Approved Safety Toe and Plate (i.e., Baffin - Derrick)
TIP: -40○C Dunlop footwear does not provide sufficient insulation when temps drop below -10○C
□ Insulated coverall or bibs. See Ontario Regulations below if working in Ontario.
□ Insulated jacket. See Ontario Regulations below if working in Ontario.
□ Personal ski gloves or gauntlet gloves for travel to and from worksite
□ Long Johns
□ Neck warmer and toque or Balaclava
WINTER JOB CHECKLIST (OPTIONAL)
□ Bama Socks or Thermal Socks
□ Winter rated sleeping bag (-25○C or colder) Refer to crew change sheet for verification
TIP: A mummy bag rated for -7○C will not be adequate during extreme freezing conditions or
during a fuel shortage or power outage.

YEAR-ROUND JOB CHECKLIST (MUST HAVE)
□ 1 pair of work boots that meet the following requirements.
→ CSA approved steel toe
→ Steel Shank
→ Recommended: Leather Hiker style work boots for Heli Jobs
→ Recommended: Metatarsal protection (Internal Met Guard)
NOTE: Metatarsal Guard is required for work underground- Rubber boot style
preferred. See boot diagram below.
NOTE: Vale (Thompson) – Vale requires that all workers on site have an internal
MET Guard boot. External MET Guard will not be accepted.

6. Dangerous goods

For safety reasons, dangerous goods must not be packed in checked or carry-on baggage, except as specifically permitted.

Most people are fit to travel by air, but special attention is required for passengers whose health problems may be exacerbated
by altitude, travel stress, hypoxia and other travel related difficulties. Our website offers important health tips and information

Airline flights may be overbooked, and there is a slight chance that a seat will not be available on a flight for which a person

If you are denied boarding, your flight is cancelled or delayed for at least two hours, or your baggage is lost or damaged, you may be

NOTICE of Liability Limitations

The Montreal Convention or the Warsaw Convention system may be applicable to your journey and these Conventions govern and
may limit the liability of air carriers for death or bodily injury, for loss of or damage to baggage, and for delay.

Where the Montreal Convention applies, the limits of liability are as follows:

1. There are no financial limits in respect of death or bodily injury.
2. In respect of destruction, loss of, or damage or delay to baggage, 1,519 Special Drawing Rights (approximately $2,800 CAD)
per passenger in most cases.
3. For damage occasioned by delay to your journey, 6,303 Special Drawing Rights (approximately $11,000 CAD) per passenger
in most cases.

Where the Warsaw Convention system applies, the following limits of liability may apply:

1. 16,600 Special Drawing Rights (approximately EUR 20,000; US $20,000) in respect of death or bodily injury if the Hague
Protocol to the Convention applies, or 8,300 Special Drawing Rights (approximately EUR 10,000; US $10,000) if only the
Warsaw Convention applies. Many carriers have voluntarily waived these limits in their entirety, and US regulations require
that, for journeys to, from or with an agreed stopping place in the US, the limit may not be less than US $75,000.
2. 17 Special Drawing Rights (approximately EUR 20; US $20) per kg for loss of or damage or delay to checked baggage and
332 Special Drawing Rights (approximately EUR 400; US $400) for unchecked baggage.
3. The carrier may also be liable for damage occasioned by delay.

Air Canada waives its limits of liability for lost, damaged and delayed mobility aids, when such items have been accepted as checked
baggage. For more information, please consult our website and our tariffs.

Where neither the Montreal Convention nor the Warsaw Convention system applies: For travel wholly between points in Canada, the
liability limit for loss or delay of, or damage to baggage is 1,519 Special Drawing Rights (approximately $2,800 CAD) per passenger.

Further information may be obtained from Air Canada as to the limits applicable to your journey. If your journey involves carriage by
different carriers, you should contact each carrier for information on the applicable limits of liability.

Regardless of which Convention applies to your journey, you may benefit from a higher limit of liability for loss of, damage or delay to
baggage by making at check-in a special declaration of the value of your baggage and paying any supplementary fee that may apply.
Alternatively, if the value of your baggage exceeds the applicable limit of liability, you should fully insure it before you travel.

Time limit for action: Any action in court to claim damages must be brought within two years from the date of arrival of the aircraft, or

6. If a carrier sells air transportation services or checks baggage specifying carriage on another carrier, it does so only as agent

HY-TECH DRILLING IS LOOKING FOR A FULL TIME PERMANENT HEALTH AND
SAFETY ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT TO JOIN OUR TEAM IN SMITHERS, BC.

ABOUT HY-TECH
Hy-Tech Drilling is an innovative, capable, and accountable diamond drilling partner for the leading mining
companies in the Americas and Europe, enabling our clients to reach critical minerals more quickly with
less environmental impact. This supports a global transition to a more sustainable future. We seek
win/win/win solutions for our people, our customers, and the communities we support.

Established in 1991, Hy-Tech has grown to a fleet of 60 drills operating throughout Canada, USA, Chile, and
Europe. We take pride in the success we’ve had working with our clients to develop innovative solutions
for their project challenges and believe in our team’s strength and effectiveness in tackling challenges that
may arise.

THE JOB
The Health & Safety Administrative Assistant provides administrative support to the Health and Safety
Department and carries out responsibilities in some or all the functional areas: Health, Safety and Training.
The position will utilize your skills in relationship building, collaboration, and communication to develop
the team, and represent Hy-Tech Drilling in a professional manner.

Responsibilities include:

• Support Health, Safety, and Training programs across the organization.
• Coordinate employee orientations, training records, and competency tracking.
• Maintain employee files, databases, and safety documentation.
• Assist with incident response processes and Health & Safety initiatives.
• Organize and support internal and external training programs and events.
• Prepare meeting agendas, take minutes, track action items, and provide administrative support to
committees.
• Monitor and process safety reports, audits, hazard identifications, and corrective actions.
• Develop, update, and distribute training materials, presentations, field resources, and employee
communications.
• Compile and analyze safety and training data to support reporting and continuous improvement.
• Manage correspondence, document filing, and departmental communications.
• Support the creation of company presentations, newsletters, and other internal communications.
• Ensure compliance with company policies, management systems, and regulatory requirements.
• Provide administrative and operational support to the Health, Safety, and Training teams,
including occasional after-hours and weekend coverage.


THE PERKS
• Competitive compensation based on experience and qualifications ($25.75 - $31.25).
• Eligible for an annual performance bonus based on company performance
• Career growth, development, and continuous learning opportunities.
• Comprehensive 100% employer-paid benefits package upon successful completion of probation.
• Progressive employer RRSP contribution program.
• Employee and family access to wellness and employee assistance programs, along with a
membership to Bulkley Valley Recreation Center.


THE SETTING
This position is based out of the Company Headquarters in Smithers, BC. Office work environment with
some travel required.
THE SCHEDULE
Standard working hours are 8am – 5pm Monday to Friday. There will also be some requirements to be
available after hours and on weekends during busy times.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS
• 2-3 years of administrative experience.
• Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
• Excellent organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
• Intermediate computer skills, including experience with spreadsheets, email, databases, and
word processing software.
• Valid Driver’s Licence and provide a current Driver’s Abstract annually.




APPLICATION DEADLINE August 7, 2026

Apply online: https://hy-techdrilling.com/our-crew/job-
HOW TO APPLY

program upon successful completion of a 3-month probationary period.
